title: E2E test suite for Hosted data residency region pinning (blocking, streaming, fallback)
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — Hosted data residency enforcement
description:
## Context
We’re rolling out Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning + deterministic request-time blocks) for Enterprise customers. Support and Sales escalations show the highest-risk regressions are:
- Region-pinned orgs accidentally routed to a disallowed region via endpoint selection or fallback.
- Streaming endpoints returning generic 500 / truncated frames instead of the standardized residency violation error.
- Cross-region fallback attempts when a region is degraded/capacity constrained.

This ticket adds an end-to-end test suite that runs against staging (and optionally prod-canary) to continuously validate residency enforcement behavior across routing + gateway + streaming.

## Goals
- Catch regressions in the full request path (gateway → policy eval → routing → response formatting).
- Validate error contract for blocked requests is consistent across streaming and non-streaming.
- Validate fallback behavior respects allowed regions and never crosses region boundaries by default.
- Provide a CI gating plan that’s strict enough to prevent shipping regressions but pragmatic about flake.

## Out of scope
- Deep verification of internal log/audit sinks (we’ll assert response-level signals and rely on unit/integration tests for internal telemetry schema).
- Multi-region replication scenarios (non-goal for initial release).

## Test environments
- Primary: staging (feature flag enabled, seeded test orgs).
- Optional: prod-canary (once allowlisted) — smoke only, no destructive config mutations.

## Owners / reviewers
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (assignee)
- API Gateway: Amara Diallo / Brian Murphy
- Routing: Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon
- Control plane: Ethan Park

## Notes on seeded test data
We will maintain 2–3 dedicated e2e orgs in staging with stable IDs and short-lived API keys created during test setup:
- org_e2e_residency_eu_only: allowed_regions=["eu-west-1"], primary_region="eu-west-1"
- org_e2e_residency_eu_multi: allowed_regions=["eu-west-1","eu-central-1"], primary_region="eu-west-1"
- org_e2e_residency_unpinned: no residency policy (control)

Policies are created/updated via Control Plane Admin API in setup, and cleaned up in teardown (best-effort).
acceptance_criteria:
- E2E tests exist for non-streaming request blocked by residency when calling a disallowed region endpoint.
- E2E tests exist for streaming request blocked by residency and returns standardized error payload/frames (no generic 500).
- E2E tests exist for fallback behavior:
  - When cross-region fallback would be required, request is blocked (default).
  - When fallback within allowed region set is possible, request succeeds and stays within allowed set.
- Tests assert:
  - HTTP status code and machine-readable error code match ADR-022.
  - request_id is present and stable across streaming/non-streaming surfaces.
  - help_url (or docs link field) present where applicable.
- CI plan implemented and documented:
  - A fast smoke subset runs on every merge to main for gateway/routing/control-plane repos touching residency.
  - Full suite runs nightly with alerting on failures.
  - Clear retry policy + flake budget; failures create an oncall-visible signal (Slack + CI annotation).
- Test suite is runnable locally by engineers with a single command and documented prerequisites (staging creds, feature flag, environment variables).
implementation_notes:
## Proposed test harness
- Repo: redwood (monorepo) under /e2e/residency/
- Runner: existing e2e runner (pytest-based) with explicit markers: @residency_smoke, @residency_full
- Auth: use a staging service token for Control Plane Admin API to create/update policies and mint API keys.
- Requests: hit explicit regional base URLs to force ‘wrong region’ scenarios (ex: https://us.api.staging.redwood.ai) and validate deterministic blocks.

## Assertions (response-level)
Blocked (non-streaming):
- status: 409 (expected for policy conflict)
- error.code: RESIDENCY_POLICY_VIOLATION (exact string per ADR)
- error.message: contains actionable guidance (e.g., "This request is not allowed in region us-east-1. Update allowed regions or use EU endpoint.")
- error.request_id present
- error.help_url present (docs)

Blocked (streaming):
- SSE/stream returns a structured error event (no partial token frames).
- The final frame includes same error.code + request_id.

Fallback:
- Induce fallback attempt by sending requests with a header/config that targets a model currently unavailable in eu-west-1 (staging-only test model), ensuring router would normally fall back.
- Assert router does not cross from EU-only into us-east-1.

## Flake mitigation
- All tests include bounded retries (2) for 5xx unrelated to residency (network / staging deploy windows).
- Residency-specific assertions must be strict: no retries on a residency mismatch (treat as regression).
- Add an explicit ‘staging ready’ check (health endpoint + feature-flag check) before executing tests.

## Data hygiene
- Policies created with a test-run identifier in description fields for auditability.
- Teardown removes policies and revokes keys; on teardown failure, log the IDs for manual cleanup.
ci_gating_plan:
## Phase 1 (now): non-blocking signal
- Add GitHub Actions job: e2e-residency-smoke (staging)
- Trigger: PRs to redwood touching:
  - gateway/ (or api-gateway)
  - routing/
  - control-plane/residency/
  - sdk error mapping (optional)
- Behavior: report status but does not block merges for the first week; collect flake rate.

## Phase 2 (after 7 days green): blocking for high-risk paths
- Make e2e-residency-smoke required for merges to main for gateway + routing + control-plane paths.
- Keep full suite nightly only.

## Nightly
- e2e-residency-full runs at 02:00 UTC.
- Failures post to #eng-sre and create a Linear incident stub if failure persists > 2 consecutive runs.

## Rollback plan
- If tests become noisy during staging instability, SRE can temporarily disable the required check via repo settings and file a follow-up ticket to restore gating once stability returns.

## Ownership
- SRE owns CI + secrets.
- Feature teams own keeping assertions aligned with ADR-022 error contract and routing policy semantics.
test_matrix:
- T1 (Non-streaming block): EU-only org, call US regional base URL → 409 + RESIDENCY_POLICY_VIOLATION + request_id.
- T2 (Non-streaming allow): EU-only org, call EU regional base URL → 200 success, response includes residency decision context header (if present).
- T3 (Streaming block): EU-only org, call US regional base URL on streaming endpoint → structured error event, no generic 500.
- T4 (Fallback blocked): EU-only org, request triggers fallback to US in normal routing → blocked with residency violation.
- T5 (Fallback allowed within EU set): EU-multi org (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), simulate eu-west-1 unavailable → succeeds in eu-central-1.
- T6 (Control): Unpinned org, call US base URL → allowed (ensures our test harness isn’t accidentally pinning all orgs).
